title: Harmful Partial Interventions and Benign Leakage in Concept-based Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.21750v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems deployed in high-risk settings increasingly require models that support meaningful human oversight. Concept-based models (CMs) offer a promising framework by enabling users to inspect and intervene on intermediate, human-understandable concepts. However, concept interventions can counterintuitively worsen downstream predictions, a failure mode we formalise as intervention harm. We distinguish harm after all concepts have been intervened on from harm under partial interventions, the more likely practical use case. Modern CMs often achieve high accuracy by encoding, or leaking, additional task-relevant information in their intermediate concept representations. Recent work argues that such leakage can be benign with respect to intervention harm when concept representations satisfy two conditions: sufficiency and localisation. translated_title: 基于概念的模型中的有害部分干预与良性泄漏
translated_abstract: 部署在高风险环境中的人工智能系统越来越需要能够支持有意义的人类监督的模型。基于概念的模型为用户提供了一个有前景的框架，使用户能够检查和干预中间的、人类可理解的概念。然而，概念干预可能会反直觉地恶化下游预测，我们将这种失败模式形式化为“干预伤害”。我们区分了在所有概念都被干预后的伤害与部分干预下的伤害，后者是更贴近实际的常见使用场景。现代概念模型通常通过在中间概念表示中编码（即泄漏）额外的任务相关信息来实现高准确率。最近的研究认为，当概念表示满足两个条件——充分性和局部化——时，这种泄漏对于干预伤害而言可以是良性的。我们证明这些标准不足以保证概念干预……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文形式化了基于概念的模型中概念干预反直觉地恶化下游预测的“干预伤害”问题，区分了全量干预与更贴近实际的部分干预两种情形，并证明“充分性”和“局部化”这两个标准不足以保证部分干预下概念泄漏是良性的。
